content: Dr. Haroon Saloojee serves as the Head of the Division of Community Paediatrics within the Department of Paediatrics and Child Health at the University of the Witwatersrand in Johannesburg, South Africa. Dr. Sadia Shakoor is an Associate Professor in Pathology, Laboratory Medicine, and Pediatrics at Aga Khan University in Karachi, Pakistan. Rachel Smith is a Senior Midwifery Advisor at the Burnet Institute in Melbourne, Australia. Dr. Joseph S. Solomkin is the Executive Director of OASIS Global, based in Cincinnati, Ohio, USA. Observers include Deborah Armbruster, a Senior Maternal and Newborn Health Advisor at the United States Agency for International Development (USAID) in Washington, D.C., and Emma Clark, a Senior Maternal Health Advisor contracted by USAID. Dr. Jeanne A. Conry, President-elect of the International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics (FIGO) and Past President of the American College of Obstetrics and Gynecology, is based in California, USA. Dr. Maria Fernanda Escobar, a FIGO representative and obstetrician/gynecologist, works at Fundación Valle del Lili in Cali, Colombia. Jeff Smith is the Deputy Director of Implementation Research and Demonstration for Scale at the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation in Seattle, Washington, USA. Ann Yates is the Lead Midwifery Advisor at the International Confederation of Midwifery in The Hague, Netherlands. The Evidence Synthesis Group (ESG) includes Dr. Edgardo Abalos, Vice Director of Centro Rosarino de Estudios Perinatales in Rosario, Argentina; Anna Cuthbert from the Cochrane Pregnancy and Childbirth Group in Liverpool, United Kingdom; and Virginia Diaz, also from Centro Rosarino de Estudios Perinatales. Katherine Eddy and Leanne Jones are Research Associates at the Cochrane Pregnancy and Childbirth Group Editorial Office at the University of Liverpool. Frances Kellie and Myfanwy Williams are Managing Editors and Research Associates, respectively, at the same institution. The External Review Group (ERG) includes Ayse Akin from the Department of Public Health at Baskent University in Ankara, Turkey, and Dr. Justus Hofmeyr from the Department of Obstetrics and Gynaecology at the University of Botswana and the University of the Witwatersrand in South Africa. Dr. Tina Lavender is affiliated with the Centre for Global Women’s Health at the University of Manchester, United Kingdom. Dr. Suneeta Mittal is part of the Department of Obstetrics and Gynaecology at Fortis Memorial Research Institute in Haryana, India. Dr. Alan Tita is a specialist in Maternal-Fetal Medicine at the University of Alabama at Birmingham, USA. Dr. Khalid Yunis is a Professor of Pediatrics and Head of Neonatology at the American University of Beirut in Lebanon. Dr. John Varallo is the Global Director of Safe Surgery at Jhpiego, an affiliate of Johns Hopkins University in Baltimore, Maryland, USA. WHO country and regional officers include Bremen De Mucio, focusing on sexual and reproductive health in the Americas, based in Montevideo, Uruguay; Karima Gholbzouri, working in the Eastern Mediterranean region in Cairo, Egypt; Chandani Anoma Jayathilaka, specializing in family health in South-East Asia, based in New Delhi, India; Oleg Kuzmenko, focusing on country health programs in Europe, based in Copenhagen, Denmark; Leopold Ouedraogo, addressing reproductive and maternal health in Africa, based in Brazzaville, Democratic Republic of the Congo; Howard Sobel, focusing on maternal and adolescent health in the Western Pacific region, based in Manila, Philippines; and Claudio Sosa, working on sexual and reproductive health in the Americas, based in Montevideo, Uruguay. The WHO Steering Group includes Mercedes Bonet, Doris Chou, Tina Lavin, Olufemi T. Oladapo, Joshua P. Vogel, and Maurice Bucagu, all of whom are involved in maternal and perinatal health research. Christine Francis is a consultant in infection prevention and control. The WHO recommendations on prophylactic antibiotics for women undergoing cesarean sections prioritize outcomes such as severe infectious morbidity (e.g., sepsis, septic shock, laparotomy, or hysterectomy due to infection), puerperal infections (e.g., endometritis), wound infections, side effects of antibiotics, and antimicrobial resistance. Additional important outcomes include maternal death, well-being, satisfaction, cost of care, neonatal mortality, and neonatal infections. These outcomes were updated to align with the current WHO maternal sepsis definition. Evidence from Cochrane systematic reviews highlights comparisons between different classes of antibiotics for cesarean section prophylaxis. The review included 39 trials, with data from 33 trials involving 8,073 women. The trials compared various antibiotic classes, including cephalosporins and penicillins, with limited evidence on their effectiveness in reducing maternal and neonatal infections. Most studies had very low certainty of evidence, and no clear benefits or harms were identified for specific antibiotic classes. The review also noted that timing of antibiotic administration (e.g., before skin incision versus after cord clamping) may influence outcomes, but further research is needed to confirm this. Women’s perspectives on cesarean section recovery emphasized concerns about pain, mobility, caregiving, and wound healing, as well as the need for better information on infection risks and prevention. In summary, the evidence on the effectiveness of different antibiotic classes for cesarean section prophylaxis remains uncertain, with limited data on maternal and neonatal outcomes. Further research is needed to address these gaps and provide clearer guidance.
